Subject: Debug log retention and deletion evidence for SOC2/SIG

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team reviewed the SIG and CAIQ you shared and has a follow-up specifically about debug/diagnostic logs. Two asks: 

1) We need to understand the maximum retention window for tenant-scoped debug traces and any available carveout options (we may need up to 90 days for a subset of tenants for regulatory reasons).
2) What concrete evidence can Redwood provide to show deletion actually occurred (proof-of-delete artifacts, manifests, deletion API logs, keystore rotation evidence)?

I've attached the portion of the SIG we annotated (bluecap_sig_questionnaire.pdf) with highlighted questions. Can you point us to the artifacts you can provide and propose a path if we need a temporary 90-day debug retention exception?

We'd like to avoid a long compliance review cycle — happy to take an agreed playbook/attestation + procurement amendment if that speeds things up.

Samantha

Head of IT Security | BlueCap Diagnostics

Date: 2026-08-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Debug log retention and deletion evidence for SOC2/SIG

Samantha — thanks for the notes and the annotated SIG. Looping in Neha (security/compliance) and Naomi (your account lead).

Short answers up front: our default tenant-scoped debug/session trace retention is 30 days. We do support customer-specific extensions; a 90-day carveout is feasible for scoped, named tenants with compensating controls and a documented attestation. For deletion proof, we can provide:

- Deletion manifests (signed by internal process) showing object ids + timestamps
- Service audit logs that capture the deletion API call and operator/service identity
- Keystore rotation logs and KMS audit trails for key revocations when relevant
- A sample proof-of-delete package (hashes + timestamped manifest) for validation

Next steps proposal: Naomi/AC team can prepare a short carveout addendum (one paragraph) and Neha can prepare an evidence checklist + sample artifacts. If BlueCap signs the attestation and we get procurement PO/DocuSign, we can enable a tenant-scoped 90-day debug retention flag within 5 business days.

Would you like a quick 30-min call tomorrow to run the checklist?

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[Sent from Redwood — mobile]

Subject: Re: Debug log retention and deletion evidence for SOC2/SIG — proposed evidence pack

Hi Samantha / team,

Thanks — below is a pragmatic evidence checklist we typically provide for retention carveouts. I'll attach a worked example matrix for BlueCap with our recommended compensating controls.

What we can deliver (examples):
- Proof-of-delete manifest: CSV with object_id, hash, deletion_timestamp, operator_id, signed by Redwood HSM process.
- Deletion API audit: service logs capturing the deletion request id, requestor, and response (immutable audit stream retained under SOC2 controls)
- Snapshot of object metadata prior to deletion (for sampling) — redacted to remove PII on request
- KMS/HSM logs: key usage and rotation events tied to the period in question (where keys were used to encrypt the persisted artifacts)
- Conditional retention policy doc: exact config we apply per-tenant (retention TTLs, retention-exempt labels)

Compensating controls for a 90-day tenant carveout (recommended):
- Tenant-level enrollment map (list of tenant ids covered by the exception)
- Quarterly access reviews for debug artifacts (reviewed and signed by BlueCap security)
- Indexed tagging + limited access role (only two named BLUECAP engineers + Redwood SRE on a read-only, time-limited role)
- Enhanced logging of any read/export operations on the retained debug traces

Delivery format: a zipped evidence bundle with sample manifest, sanitized logs, and a short attestation template that BlueCap can sign (DocuSign). I attached the retention matrix we will fill out for your tenant set (redwood-retention-matrix.xlsx).

A couple of clarifying asks for BlueCap so we can scope the artifact delivery: 
- Which tenant IDs need the 90-day carveout (or do you prefer "environment" scope like prod-only)?
- Is BlueCap comfortable with us redacting PII in sample artifacts, or do you need raw (we can accommodate with an NDA/justified access list)?

If you confirm the scope I'll prepare the attestation language and a sample proof-of-delete package you can validate.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-retention-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]
